items.title: A bounded above inverse system of derived objects with compatible reduction is derived complete and recovers each term by reduction
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement takes a ring A, an ideal I, objects K_n of the derived categories of the quotients A over I^n with compatible transition maps, and three hypotheses (Noetherianity, boundedness above, and the reduction isomorphisms), and concludes both that the derived limit K is derived complete and that reducing K modulo I^n recovers K_n (statement lines 28470-28483). The proof combines a general criterion with an explicit construction: derived completeness comes from the criterion on derived limits, while the second assertion requires choosing bounded above complexes of free modules over each quotient and lifting the transition maps so that the reductions are honest isomorphisms of complexes, after which K is the limit of the system and that limit is a bounded above complex of flat modules, so that the reductions can be computed termwise and the system stabilizes at the n-th term (proof lines 28485-28516). The stabilization step is what makes the reduction of K isomorphic to K_n, and it depends on the strictness of the lifted maps. The counted span refers three times to results of this chapter and twice more to items of the same chapter, all carried as navigation stubs.
